methods.label: Find an altitude, then compare areas
methods.explanation:
The midpoint \(M\) lets us find a right triangle inside the equilateral triangle. Since \(AB=BC\), the segment from \(B\) to the midpoint \(M\) of \(AC\) is perpendicular to \(AC\). Also, \(CM=1\) and \(BC=2\). The Pythagorean theorem in right \(\triangle BMC\) gives
\[
BM=\sqrt{BC^2-CM^2}
=\sqrt{2^2-1^2}
=\sqrt3.
\]
Using \(CM\) as the base and \(BM\) as the height, the area of \(\triangle BCM\) is
\[
\frac12\cdot1\cdot\sqrt3=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
To transfer this area to the requested triangle, use \(BC\) and \(CD\) as bases. Because \(C\) is the midpoint of \(BD\), these bases are equal and lie on the same line. Both triangles \(BCM\) and \(CDM\) have vertex \(M\), so they have the same altitude to that line and therefore equal areas. Thus the area of \(\triangle CDM\) is \(\boxed{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
